description: The hand-verified expected outcome for oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/malformed-dependency-check.json -- a document written under a KNOWN artifact name whose content is not that writer's native shape. It states a HALT, not rows, despite the .rows.json suffix this folder's naming convention requires: the suffix names the folder's contract (one expected file per fixture), not the shape of every outcome. Every value below was derived by reading the fixture and the authored tables in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py, and each is asserted programmatically by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/test_shape_routing_negative.py rather than taken on trust.
tool_note: The tool IS resolved here, which is what distinguishes this fixture from expected/unknown-shape.rows.json: the name routing keys on is one of the nine, so the writer is known and only its document shape is wrong. The canonical identifier is the runner and artifact stem dependency-check, never a product name such as OWASP Dependency-Check.
null_field_note: scanner_class and adapter are null rather than omitted, so a generic loader reads this file with the same keys as the positive expected files in this folder. They are null because the halt precedes adapter selection and row construction; dependency-check rows would otherwise carry the fixed class vuln.

fixture.authored_note: An authored document, not captured tool output. It carries the envelope members a real Dependency-Check report opens with -- reportSchema, scanInfo, projectInfo -- and omits the one member the signature requires: there is no dependencies key at all. That is the plausible mis-shape for this artifact, because a report truncated by a failed analysis, or an envelope emitted before the dependency section was written, looks exactly like this. Nothing in it is a finding, a coordinate, a CVE, a credential or a token, and no value is a measurement of anything.
fixture.why_it_is_not_named_dependency_check_jso: This folder already holds fixtures/dependency-check.json, the captured positive fixture, so a second file cannot take that name. The negative test therefore routes this document under the artifact filename its writer uses (see routed_as below) rather than under the fixture's own filename, which resolves to no tool at all.

routed_as.subject: dependency-check.json
routed_as.second_subject_note: Both forms are asserted, because a run resolves the path form (shape.route_artifact over an entry in harness/artifacts/raw/) while a bare filename is what the authored tables hold. Only the filename component is read; neither path is opened, and no absolute path appears in this file or in the test.
routed_as.fixture_name_resolution_note: shape.resolve_tool("malformed-dependency-check.json") is None. Asserted by the test so the halt below cannot be passing for the wrong reason: routed under its own name this document would halt with shape.REASON_UNRECOGNIZED_ARTIFACT_NAME, a different condition owned by expected/unknown-shape.rows.json. The assertion matters more for this writer than for any other, because the fixture name ENDS in the artifact stem -- a resolver matching on a suffix rather than on the whole stem would resolve it, and the assertion pins that it does not.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Recorded for parity with the positive expected files in this folder; no row below carries it, because rows is empty by expectation.

shape_detection.conjunction: isinstance(doc, Mapping) and doc.get("version") == "2.1.0" and isinstance(doc.get("runs"), list)
shape_detection.is_sarif_derivation: A mapping with no version key and no runs key: None == "2.1.0" is False and isinstance(None, list) is False, so both halves fail and the native signature below is the test that decides this document's fate. The document does carry a reportSchema member, which is a version-shaped field under a different name -- the SARIF test reads the key version and nothing else, so a schema declaration of any other name cannot make a native report look like SARIF.

native_signature.authority: normalize.shape.NATIVE_SIGNATURES["dependency-check"], derived from AAP 0.5.4's per-shape record-location table
native_signature.expected: a JSON object carrying "dependencies" whose value is a JSON array, each element one scanned dependency holding its vulnerabilities. An empty array is legitimate, and so is a report whose every dependency carries no vulnerability at all
native_signature.expected_note: Recorded verbatim and asserted equal to the signature's own statement string, so this file cannot describe a requirement the implementation does not make.
native_signature.why_it_fails: The top-level type is right and the envelope reads like a real report, but the container the record location depends on is absent entirely, so the dependencies[].vulnerabilities[] path the adapter walks and reconcile._count_dependency_check counts has no first segment. observed_key_type is the literal absent rather than null, so the halt message distinguishes a key that is missing from a key that is present holding JSON null.
native_signature.what_is_deliberately_not_required: The signature reads nothing inside dependencies. An empty array is legitimate -- it is what the report carries when the scan resolved no dependency at all, which is the expected outcome for a scan whose in-scope surface holds no package manifest -- and so is a dependency element carrying no vulnerabilities array. Neither reportSchema, scanInfo nor projectInfo is required, so an envelope member added or renamed by a later Dependency-Check version cannot invalidate an otherwise valid report.

counting_traversal.note: This is the measured reason the halt has to exist. _count_dependency_check reads dependencies through its own tolerant accessor, which yields an empty tuple for an absent key, so it returns zero -- and an adapter reading the same absent key would emit zero rows and zero rejections. Before this fix the identity balanced at 0 = 0 + 0 over a truncated report and parse status read clean, which is the most dangerous instance of the defect for this particular tool: zero rows is ALSO the expected honest outcome here, since the twelve in-scope globs carry no dependency manifest, so a truncated report would have been absorbed into an expected result without a trace. AAP 0.5.4 requires a halt rather than a best-effort parse, and AAP 0.9.2 lists the condition among those that stop the run.
counting_traversal.traversal_unchanged: reconcile.py's traversal is deliberately not hardened into a second shape test: its value is that it shares no code and no judgement with the row builder. The halt belongs one layer up, in shape.py.

named_halt_requirement.statement: A KeyError or TypeError escaping a half-attempted parse is a FAILURE, not a pass: it carries no reason, names no artifact, quotes no expected signature and cannot be told apart from a defect in the normalizer itself. KeyError is named first for this artifact because an absent container is precisely what a subscript-based reader raises on. The test asserts the exact type with assertIs(type(error), shape.UnknownArtifactShape), never Exception.
named_halt_requirement.raised_by_the_shape_layer: The exception must come from normalize.shape.route or normalize.shape.route_artifact -- the module that owns the decision -- rather than from an adapter reached with a document whose shape was never established.

halt.reason_inventory: shape.HALT_REASONS, the closed set of four: unrecognized-artifact-name, unsupported-document-type, sarif-producer-artifact-not-sarif, native-shape-unrecognized.
halt.reason_note: Not the name reason: the name resolves to dependency-check. Not the container reason: an object top level is a supported container. The halt is attributable to the document not being this writer's native shape.
halt.raised_before: any adapter module is named, imported or called, and before any record traversal of any kind

observed_attributes.stem_note: For this reason the stem carries the canonical tool identifier rather than a filename: the writer is known by the time the signature is tested. For this writer the two coincide, which is why the fixture-name assertion above is asserted separately.

message_must_carry: the observed structure where that signature required a container, naming the required key and reporting it absent
halt.details_method: shape.UnknownArtifactShape.details() returns the same facts as a flat JSON-serialisable mapping, adding expected_artifacts, signature_tool, expected_signature and signature_observation. The test asserts json.dumps over it succeeds, because harness/artifacts/logs/normalize-run.json has to carry the halt record.

not_a_rejection.reject_classes_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_CLASSES tuple -- a closed set of ten class names, not copied here so the one authority cannot drift into two.
not_a_rejection.statement: The stated outcome is a halt, not a counted rejection: a rejection is a per-record outcome inside an adapter that already owns its artifact, and this document never reaches an adapter. The test asserts the non-membership of the reason and the exception name over paths.REJECT_CLASSES programmatically.

halt.reason_literal_divergence: This value was authored as the literal 'native-signature-mismatch' against a tree where the signature check owned a reason of its own. In the delivered tree that constant and shape.REASON_NATIVE_SHAPE_UNRECOGNIZED are ONE literal -- 'native-shape-unrecognized' -- because a known artifact name whose document does not carry that writer's structure is one condition however it is detected, and two literals for it would put a reason outside shape.HALT_REASONS, which the router's own inventory is asserted closed over. reason_constant is unchanged and is what the test compares against; the literal recorded here is the value that constant holds in this tree.

parse.why_well_formedness_is_the_point: A document that fails to parse is stopped by the parser and no shape decision is reached. It is precisely a document that parses perfectly, carries a known artifact name and reads plausibly that tempts a best-effort parse -- and a truncated report that still closes its braces is the most plausible such document of all.

counts.raw_count_unit_note: Null rather than 0: a count unit is a property of a document of the right shape, and this document has none. What the traversal would return over it anyway is recorded above under counting_traversal.would_return, where it is evidence about the defect rather than a reconciliation figure.
counts.reconciliation_identity: not applicable -- the halt precedes any record traversal, so no count unit exists to reconcile against

rows_note: Explicitly empty, and empty for a different reason than a clean scan is empty: the pipeline stopped, it did not look and find nothing.
guarded_failure: A permissive shape layer does not raise on this document -- it hands it to the dependency-check adapter, which finds no dependencies container, emits zero rows and zero rejections and reports success. The independent counting traversal returns zero as well, so the identity balances and parse status reads clean. For this tool the resulting dataset evidence is indistinguishable from the run's genuinely expected outcome, since no dependency manifest sits inside the twelve scope globs -- which is exactly why the halt has to be raised by shape, at a layer that reads the document rather than the count.

assertions: shape.route over this fixture's parsed document under the subject dependency-check.json raises shape.UnknownArtifactShape, and the raised type is exactly that class.
shape.route_artifact over harness/artifacts/raw/dependency-check.json and the same document raises the same reason, so both entry points halt.
error.reason equals shape.REASON_NATIVE_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH, and is neither of the other two members of shape.HALT_REASONS.
error.signature_tool is dependency-check and error.expected_signature equals shape.NATIVE_SIGNATURES["dependency-check"].statement, which this file records verbatim.
error.signature_observation records the required key, the required type and the observed type absent, and those match the values recorded here.
shape.is_sarif over the document is False and shape.matches_native_signature("dependency-check", doc) is False.
shape.matches_native_signature("dependency-check", {"dependencies": []}) is True, so a report that resolved no dependency at all still routes.
reconcile.count_records("dependency-check", doc) is 0 -- the false-clean this halt prevents, asserted rather than asserted about.
No adapter module is imported by the halting routing call.
The rows array is empty, the rejection total is 0, and neither the reason nor the exception name is a member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES.
shape.resolve_tool over the fixture's own filename is None, so the subject the test routes under is the artifact filename and not the fixture name.
The fixture's sha256, byte size, top-level type and top-level keys equal the values recorded here, so this file cannot drift from the document it describes.
negative_test_contract.mandated_direction_note: AAP 0.5.4 mandates a negative test asserting that a native artifact does not route to the SARIF adapter; that assertion is owned by the same test file over the captured native fixtures. This fixture extends it in the direction the review found open: a KNOWN filename whose content is not that writer's native shape must halt rather than become a clean zero-result.

related_fixtures.the_captured_positive: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/dependency-check.json -- the report this document imitates, whose dependencies IS an array and which routes normally.
related_fixtures.the_legitimate_empty_case: No fixture file: the legitimate empty document for this writer is asserted inline by the test as {"dependencies": []}, because the honest zero-dependency report is one key wide and a committed file would document nothing the assertion does not.
related_fixtures.the_fall_through: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/unknown-shape.json -- a document under an UNRECOGNISED name, which halts for a different reason.
related_fixtures.note: Named so a reader can see which layer owns which failure. No fixture's outcome is inferred from another's, and each expected file states its own.

prohibitions_observed: No secret value, credential, token or connection string appears in any field of this file or its fixture (this tree is committed to git), and no NVD API key or Sonatype OSS Index credential is named or implied. No finding is judged, nothing is deduplicated, and no tool's output is characterised against another's: this file describes one document's shape decision and the halt it must produce, and nothing else.
